title: Account engagement slate: SMB + Enterprise QBR templates (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects two parallel QBR slide slates and an accompanying lightweight renewal tracker: one optimized for SMB accounts (short, impact-focused) and one for Enterprise accounts (longer, exec + technical threads). Aim: give CSMs a modular deck they can remix quickly and a minimal tracker to drive renewal conversations.

Audience and usage notes:
- Primary: CSMs running QBRs, renewal managers, AE partners.
- Secondary: Solutions Engineers (for enterprise technical deep dives), RevOps (for metrics alignment).
- Version: draft — feedback requested in #cs-qbr Slack thread or PR to the templates repo.

High-level differences (SMB vs Enterprise):
- SMB: 20–30 min, 8–10 slides, focus on usage, value highlights, quick wins, simple renewal ask.
- Enterprise: 45–60 min, 15–20 slides, includes deep reliability/ops section, roadmap alignment, security/compliance slide, detailed renewal options and multi-year incentives.

SMB slate (concise, adaptable) — Slide list + speaker notes (short bullets):
1) Title + meeting objectives
   - "QBR: 30 minutes — align on value and next 90 days"
   - Speaker note: call out renewal window if within 90d (quick flag).
2) Quick wins since last touch (3 bullets, metrics)
   - e.g., "Avg latency reduced 18% after model switch; token cost -12%"
3) Top 3 usage metrics (last 30/90 days)
   - Sessions, tokens per session, error rate
4) Adoption snapshot (teams, routes, top apps)
5) Business outcomes mapped to product usage
   - Short case bullet: what feature drove what outcome
6) Risk & open items (1 slide)
   - Highlight blockers and CSM asks (escalations, SE time)
7) Renewal pulse + options (1 slide)
   - Present 1–2 recommended options (e.g., 12-mo standard, prepaid commit + discount)
8) Action items & owners (1 slide)
   - Next steps with due dates

SMB speaker guidance: be crisp. Default deck time: 20–25 minutes + 5–10 mins for Qs. Use single-slide visuals, avoid heavy technical content.

Enterprise slate (expanded) — Slide list + speaker notes:
1) Title + meeting outcomes (exec + tech threads)
2) Executive summary: quantifiable impact (top-line benefit)
3) Strategic alignment: how Redwood maps to their initiatives
4) Usage & performance trends (90–180 day charts)
   - Include latency percentiles, token cost trends, tail latency incidents
5) Reliability & incidents recap (ops)
   - Past incidents, MTTR, mitigations, change in SLOs
6) Security & compliance status
   - Data residency, KMS/HSM, audit log health, outstanding items
7) Architecture snapshot + integrations in use
   - Which models, deployment modes (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), network topology notes
8) Cost efficiency and recommendations
   - Batch/quantization suggestions, estimated $/1000 tokens savings
9) Feature adoption & roadmap alignment
   - Requested features, estimated delivery windows (if applicable)
10) Risk register & mitigation plan (scored)
11) Renewal options & commercial levers
   - Multi-year discounts, dedicated capacity commitments, professional services options
12) Negotiation playbook (CS + AE coordination)
13) Action items, owners, and executive asks

Speaker guidance: prepare an appendix of supporting slides (dumps of raw metrics, incident timelines, config snippets). For enterprise accounts, always bring an SE and the AE for contractual conversations.

Slide templates: what to include per slide (copy/paste snippets CSMs can use)
- Executive summary: 3 bullets — impact, risk, ask. Visual: 1 KPI strip (ARR impact / uptime / avg latency).
- Usage chart slide: top left - metric name; center - line chart; bottom - 3 bullet observations.
- Reliability slide: timeline of incidents with root cause and key remediation.
- Roadmap alignment: two-column table (Customer goal | Redwood features / deliverables).
- Renewal slide (SMB): price band + 1-line rationale for each band.
- Renewal slide (Enterprise): pricing options, SLA add-ons, recommended negotiation cadence (e.g., 90d presales prep).

Lightweight renewal tracker (text table to paste into sheet) — columns and sample rows:
- Columns: Account, ARR, Renewal date, Renewal owner, Risk score (0–10), Primary blocker, Proposed option, AE contact, Next milestone, Last touch date, Notes
- Sample row: "Acme Corp | $48,000 | 2025-06-15 | Jordan Patel | 6 | Dedicated GPU latency | Maria Lopez | Exec review 2025-04-10 | 2025-03-01 | Need SE timing"

Risk scoring rubric (0–10) quick reference:
- 0–3: Green (low risk) — consistent usage, exec sponsor engaged, SLA met
- 4–6: Yellow (moderate) — rising cost, feature gaps, one-off incidents
- 7–10: Red (high) — churn signals: budget freeze, security blockers, major recurring outages

Pre-meeting prep checklist (CSM):
- Run token/latency report (last 90d) and attach two slides
- Confirm SE availability for technical deep dive (if enterprise)
- Check renewal window and pricing options with AE
- Circulate pre-read (1 pager) 5 business days before meeting
- Add internal prep meeting 30–60 mins before QBR

Post-meeting follow-up templates (short):
- Quick recap email (to customer):
  Subject: QBR recap + agreed next steps
  Body: "Thanks for your time — attached is the one-pager and the action list. Key next steps: 1) SE to scope latency remediation (owner/ETA), 2) AE to share contract option A/B. We'll reconvene on [date]."

- Internal follow-up (CS->AE->SE):
  "From: CSM
   TL;DR: Risk score X, agreed items: SE scope, pricing option chosen Y. Need AE to confirm commercial language by DATE."

Negotiation playbook (brief):
- Early signals: start AE involvement when risk score >=5 or renewal <120d
- Discount guardrails: Tiered discounts linked to committed GPU hours or multi-year term
- Escalation path: open CS-### Jira for technical blockers; add RevOps for special billing terms

Appendix: reusable snippets and checklists (copyable)
- 1-line renewal asks (SMB): "Renew for 12 months at current rate + 5% overcommit discount if paid upfront"
- SE handoff template: "Customer, problem, logs, sample request, suggested mitigation"
- Slide build checklist: all charts have source note, axis labels, date ranges called out

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a one-slide pricing sensitivity visual (ask RevOps for modeled scenarios) — TODO @Avery
- Finalize legal-friendly language for multi-year commitments (need counsel review) — TODO @Riley
- Create quick script for 20-min SMB QBR (speaker timing per slide) — TODO @Priya

References and links to canonical assets:
- QBR framework (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/QBR+Framework
- Templates repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cs-templates
- Slack: #cs-qbr (use thread titled "template feedback")

Notes on distribution and packaging:
- Produce two Google Slides exports: "SMB QBR — editable" and "Enterprise QBR — editable" using these slide bullets. Keep a plain-text one-pager with the renewal tracker CSV for RevOps uploads.

Quick changelog (doc history):
- 2025-02-15: initial draft assembled from CSM interviews
- 2025-02-25: added enterprise negotiation playbook (Avery)
- 2025-03-05: updated tracker columns and sample row (Priya)

Feedback welcome — please comment in the doc OR drop suggestions in #cs-qbr.

(End draft)
